XXVI.|OF THE APOSTLES.|365}}</noinclude>haue brought him forth to you, and especially to thee, king Agrippa, that examination being made, I may haue vvhat to vvrite. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=27}}† For it seemeth to me vvithout reason, to send a prisoner, & not to signifie {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''τὰς κατ ἀυτοῦ αἰτίας.''}}∷ his causes.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXVI.}}}}}}

{{c|''In that honorable Audience being permitted to speake, 2 he declareth to the king vvhat he first vvas, 12 and hovv miraculously he vvas conuerted, 19 and that he hath preached since, as he vvas commaunded from heauen, and as the Prophets had foretold of Christ. 24 Which strange tale Festus the Heathen President hearing, saith that he is mad. 25 But he ansvvereth, and exhorteth them al to be Christians as he is. 30 They finally pronounce that he might be set at libertie, but only for his appeale.''}} {{dropinitial|B|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial B, heads among foliage.png|imgsize=235px|fl={{verse|chapter=26|verse=1}}}}VT Agrippa said to Paul, Thou art permitted to speake for thy self. Then Paul stretching forth his hand, began to make his ansvver. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=2}}† Touching al things vvhereof I am accused of the Iewes, king Agrippa, I account my self happie for that I am to defend my self this day before thee, {{verse|chapter=26|verse=3}}† especially vvhereas thou knovvest al things that are among the Ievves, customes and questions: for the vvhich cause I beseeche thee, heare me patiently. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=4}}† And my life truely from my youth, vvhich vvas from the beginning in my nation in Hierusalem, al the Ievves doe knovv: {{verse|chapter=26|verse=5}}† knovving me before from the beginning (if they vvil giue testimonie) that according to the most sure {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ἁίρεσιν''}}∷ secte of our religion I liued a Pharisee. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=6}}† And novv for the hope of the promisse that vvas made of God to our fathers, doe I stand subiect to iudgement: {{verse|chapter=26|verse=7}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''b in quam''}}∷ the vvhich, our tvvelue tribes {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''λατρεῦον''}}∷ seruing night and day, hope to come vnto. Of the vvhich hope, o king, I am accused of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=8}}† Vvhat incredible thing is it iudged vvith you, if God raise the dead? {{verse|chapter=26|verse=9}}† And my self truely had thought that I ought to doe against the name of {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth many contrarie things. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=10}}† Vvhich also I {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 8, 3.''}}* did at Hierusalem, and many of the saincts did I shut vp in prisons, hauing receiued authoritie of the cheefe priests: and vvhen they vvere put to death, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''c detuli sententiam.''}}∷ I brought the sentence. {{verse|chapter=26|verse=11}}† And through out al the synagogs often times punishing them, I compelled them to blaspheme:<noinclude>{{rh||Zz iij|and}}</noinclude>
